description: Cover Parameters.swift rejection paths by driving Parameter.set directly

asi.finding: MAJOR: throwing anywhere inside a render/compute pass aborts the process (SIGABRT). The pass's workloadExit never runs, the encoder is released without endEncoding, Metal asserts in -[_MTLCommandEncoder dealloc]. Filed #357.
asi.technique: Error paths that throw mid-pass CANNOT be tested through OffscreenRenderer/Runner - the test process dies. Instead build an MTLRenderCommandEncoder/MTLComputeCommandEncoder in the test, get a Reflection from device.makeRenderPipelineState(descriptor:options:.bindingInfo), call Parameter.set(on:reflection:) directly, and end the encoder in a defer.
asi.gotcha: device.makeComputePipelineState(function:options:) resolves to the async overload; use the descriptor form to get reflection synchronously.
asi.parameters_swift: 27 -> 13 uncovered. What is left is preconditionFailure traps (ambiguous parameter, encoder mismatch) which cannot be tested, and the missing-reflection throw which needs the element tree and so is blocked on #357.
asi.per_line_tool: xcrun llvm-cov show .build/out/Products/Debug/MetalSprocketsTests.xctest/Contents/MacOS/MetalSprocketsTests -instr-profile=.build/out/Products/Debug/codecov/default.profdata <source file> | rg '^ *[0-9]+\| *0\|' shows exactly which lines are uncovered

description: Host RenderView through ViewInspector's ViewHosting, plus the no-System body path

asi.big_win: ViewHosting.host(view:size:) actually instantiates the SwiftUI view tree, so RenderView's body, RenderViewHelper's update closure, ViewModelBox and ViewAdaptor's makeNSView/updateNSView all run. +113 covered lines from one small test - by far the best return of the session.
asi.why_it_works: Everything behind a SwiftUI body or a Representable is unreachable by constructing values; it needs a host. ViewInspector's ViewHosting provides one without a window server.
asi.pattern: ViewHosting.host(view: v, size: CGSize(...)); defer { ViewHosting.expel() }. Expelling should also drive the dismantle path.
asi.next_targets: Parameters 13 (traps), StateBox 12 (traps), Error 12 (fatalError bodies), System+Snapshot 11 (unreachable Mirror fallback), Support 11 (fatalError + zero-encode branch), ComputePass 10 and RenderPass 9 (visionOS-only code, not compiled on macOS), FrameTiming 10, Logging 8, BodylessElement 7
asi.ceiling_note: A large share of what remains is deliberately unreachable: fatalError/preconditionFailure bodies, defensive Mirror fallbacks, and #if os(visionOS) blocks. Do not manufacture tests for those.

description: Host FrameTimingView across its option sets

asi.result: FrameTimingView 39.2% -> ~95%; +77 lines. Hosting is confirmed as the key to any SwiftUI body in this repo.
asi.honesty_note: ViewInspector cannot read state back out of a hosted view without adding an Inspection hook to the library source, which is not worth doing. So the hosted tests assert the body evaluates and finds its TimelineView, while the actual readout values are asserted directly against the pure rows(for:options:targetFramesPerSecond:) function. Do not swap those pure assertions for hosted ones - the hosted variant looks stronger and checks less.

description: Cover visible-function-table setup paths (no reflection yet, wrong function type)

asi.only_plus_3: Small gain: most of VisibleFunctionTableModifier's uncovered lines are throws from workloadEnter, which cannot be reached without tripping #357.
asi.key_distinction: SETUP-phase throws are safe to test through a real renderer (no encoder exists yet); WORKLOAD-phase throws abort the process. That is the rule for deciding whether an error path is testable end-to-end.
asi.near_miss: First version of the wrong-function-type test passed for the wrong reason: the pipeline failed earlier with 'Vertex function has input attributes but no vertex descriptor was set'. Always check WHICH error came back, not just that something threw.

description: Cover state-box teardown pruning and the bodyless-element phase defaults

asi.covered: StateBox.valueDidChange with a released system and with a pruned weak dependency; BodylessElement's default setupEnter/workloadEnter bodies; the unconstrained requiresSetup default reaching isEqual
asi.subtlety: requiresSetup has two implementations: a `where Self: Equatable` overload and an unconstrained default. System compares elements through a generic helper that only knows BodylessElement, so the UNCONSTRAINED one runs even for Equatable types, and it is the one that calls isEqual. Testing it means going through System.update, not calling requiresSetup directly.
asi.wrong_assumption_corrected: A non-Equatable bodyless element always returns true from requiresSetup - it does not structurally compare. My first test asserted the opposite and failed, which is the test doing its job.
asi.status: 5008 -> 5261 (+253, 87.6% -> 92.0%) over 8 iterations. Remaining top files are dominated by unreachable-by-design code.

description: Reach the mesh pipeline cache hit and linked functions, and snapshot a non-state-box property

asi.cache_key_gotcha: IMPORTANT: pipeline caches are keyed on ObjectIdentifier(MTLFunction). Building a fresh ShaderLibrary per render creates new function objects, so the cache always misses and the hit path stays uncovered. Build the shaders once and pass them into both renders. The earlier mesh 'cache hit' test was not hitting the cache at all.
asi.covered: MeshRenderPipeline cache-hit early return incl. cached depth-stencil state, mesh/object/fragment linked functions, and SystemSnapshot's non-StateBox persisted-value branch (reached with a custom MSDynamicProperty that persists a plain Int)

description: Cover shader type mismatches and render pipeline cache/stencil paths (re-measured after a noisy run)

asi.MEASUREMENT_IS_NOISY: The same tree measured 5209 then 5281 then 5282 within minutes. Swing is roughly 70 lines, which is far bigger than a typical iteration's gain (8-20). Do NOT discard a change on a single down measurement - re-run first.
asi.noise_source: Almost certainly the ViewHosting tests: whether a hosted RenderView actually gets a frame drawn depends on the run loop, and that decides whether draw(in:) and the System phases execute. When it does not draw, ~70 lines across RenderView/RenderViewSupport go uncovered.
asi.implication: Confidence scores logged for iterations 2-9 were computed against a noise floor from before the hosting tests existed, so they were optimistic. Treat anything under ~70 lines as unproven from a single run.

asi.reminder: Pipeline caches key on ObjectIdentifier(MTLFunction) - share shader instances across renders or the cache-hit path is never reached

description: Measure the median of three runs and report the spread

asi.infrastructure_only: No test or source change in this iteration; the metric is unchanged (5282 -> 5281 is noise). measure.sh now runs the suite 3x and reports the median, plus a new sample_spread metric.
asi.why: Iteration 10 measured 5209 on one run and 5281/5282 on the next two of the identical tree. Comparing single runs was no longer meaningful when iteration gains are 8-20 lines.
asi.how_to_read_spread: sample_spread is max-min across the 3 samples. Small (0-2) means the number is trustworthy. Large (~70) means the hosted-view tests did not all draw and the median may still be off - re-run before drawing conclusions.
asi.cost: ~16s per measurement with a warm build (3 test runs), vs ~8s for one.
asi.override: COVERAGE_RUNS=1 ./.auto/measure.sh for a quick look while iterating.
